Important FAQs on Data Protection & Privacy

fixes.confirmEvidence: Art. 11(3)(a): a Resident Person is "A juridical person that is incorporated or otherwise established or recognised under the applicable legislation of the State". Art. 53(1): return "no later than (9) nine months from the end of the relevant Tax Period".
fixes.note: The nine-month deadline is confirmed in the law. No official page names offshore companies; their inclusion still rests on the resident-person definition (incorporated under UAE legislation). The RAK ICC site, which has a corporate tax page, refused automated access (Incapsula bot check).

fixes.penalty: No separate penalty is set for the election itself. It is made in the corporate tax return, so a late return attracts the late-filing penalty: Late corporate tax return: AED 500 for each month or part of a month for the first twelve months, then AED 1,000 for each month or part of a month from the thirteenth month, counted from the day after the filing deadline (Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023, item 7).
fixes.penaltyEvidence: "Failure of the Registrant to submit a Tax Return within the timeframe specified in the Corporate Tax Law. 1. 500 for each month, or part thereof, for the first twelve months. 2. 1,000 for each month, or part thereof, from the thirteenth month onwards."
fixes.note: Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023 has no item for the Small Business Relief election as such; the figures are those for a late corporate tax return.

fixes.penalty: The disclosure is filed with the corporate tax return (Art. 55(1) of the law). Late corporate tax return: AED 500 for each month or part of a month for the first twelve months, then AED 1,000 for each month or part of a month from the thirteenth month, counted from the day after the filing deadline (Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023, item 7). An incorrect return: AED 500, unless corrected before the filing deadline (item 9).
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Item 9: "The Registrant submits an incorrect Tax Return. 500, unless the Person corrects his Tax Return before the expiry of the deadline for the submission of the Tax Return according to the Corporate Tax Law."
fixes.note: Art. 55(1) of the Corporate Tax Law: the Authority may require a Taxable Person "to file together with their Tax Return a disclosure" on related-party transactions. No penalty specific to the disclosure was found.

fixes.penalty: Failure to keep the records required by the Corporate Tax Law (which, in Art. 55(2), requires a master file and local file where the conditions are met): AED 10,000 for each violation, or AED 20,000 for each repeated violation within 24 months of the last one. Failure to submit tax records and documents in Arabic when requested: AED 5,000 (Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023, items 1 and 2).
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Item 1: "Failure ... to keep the required records and other information specified in the Tax Procedures Law and the Corporate Tax Law. ... 1. 10,000 for each violation. 2. 20,000 in each case of repeated violation within 24 months"
fixes.note: The decision has no separate item for handing the files over late after the 30-day request period; the general record-keeping item is the one that names records required by the Corporate Tax Law.
FTA Decision No. 5 of 2025, Art. 10: confirmation within nine months of the end of the tax period (31 December 2025 for tax periods ended on or before 31 March 2025).
fixes.notFound: No penalty for a late or missing annual confirmation is named. Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023 has items for tax returns, registration and "a Declaration ... as required in accordance with the provisions of the Corporate Tax Law" (item 13: AED 500 a month for twelve months, then AED 1,000 a month), but no official page read says item 13 covers the family foundation annual confirmation, which FTA Decision No. 5 of 2025 sets by decision rather than calling it a declaration.

fixes.penalty: Cabinet Decision No. 142 of 2024 applies Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Law (penalties are those set under the Tax Procedures Law and its implementing decisions) to the top-up tax. Transitional relief: for fiscal years beginning on or before 31 December 2026 (but not a fiscal year ending after 30 June 2028), no penalties or sanctions apply to the filing of a Top-up Tax Return or Pillar Two Information Return where the FTA considers the group took reasonable measures to apply the rules correctly. No penalty amounts specific to the top-up tax were found.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Art. 14.3: "no penalties or sanctions shall apply in connection with the filing of a Top-up Tax Return or the Pillar Two Information Return where the Federal Tax Authority considers that an MNE Group has taken reasonable measures"
fixes.note: Art. 14.2(b) of the decision says a reference to Corporate Tax includes the top-up tax, which suggests the corporate tax penalty decision (Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023) applies, but no official page says so expressly; no amounts are given here for that reason.

fixes.notFound: Optional application with no deadline. Ministerial Decision No. 247 of 2023 contains no penalty provision, and no official page states any consequence other than not having a certificate.

Optional registration with no deadline. The FTA registration page and the penalty decisions read set penalties only for late registration by persons required to register; none applies to an optional registration.

fixes.penalty: Late payment of contributions: an additional amount of 0.1% of the outstanding contributions for each day of delay, charged without warning or notice and capped at the amount of the outstanding contributions. Contributions not paid on the actual salary: an extra 10% of the outstanding contributions. Late registration of a UAE national (due within 30 days of joining): AED 200 for each day of delay. (Federal Decree-Law No. 57 of 2023, Art. 11.)
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Art. 11(4): "If the employer delays paying the contribution amount, an additional amount at 0.1% of the outstanding contributions for each day delayed will be charged, without warning or notice. In all cases, the additional amount should not exceed the value of outstanding contributions."
fixes.note: Federal Decree-Law No. 57 of 2023 applies to Emiratis who start work on or after 31 October 2023; those registered earlier stay under Federal Law No. 7 of 1999, whose English copy on gpssa.gov.ae is a scanned image and could not be read. The GPSSA Board may grant exemptions from the additional amount.

fixes.confirmEvidence: "The employers in the UAE are liable to mandatory subscriptions for their GCC employees according to the social security law in their home countries in terms of registration and subscriptions"
fixes.note: The GPSSA page also says the employer share may not exceed the share set for UAE nationals, and lists each GCC country's rates and bank accounts.
fixes.notFound: The GPSSA page sends late-payment consequences to each home country's social security law, which was not read. The executive rules (Cabinet Resolution No. 18 of 2007) are published only in Arabic on gpssa.gov.ae and were not read.

The u.ae end-of-service page states no penalty for late or unpaid gratuity. mohre.gov.ae reset the connection on every attempt (several tries during the session), and the u.ae copies of the labour law and MoHRE resolutions returned HTTP 404; no other official page read states it.

The u.ae page gives the 15-day transfer rule but no penalty; Cabinet Resolution No. 96 of 2023 and Ministerial Resolution No. 668 of 2023 on u.ae returned HTTP 404. mohre.gov.ae reset the connection on every attempt (several tries during the session), and the u.ae copies of the labour law and MoHRE resolutions returned HTTP 404; no other official page read states it.

fixes.penalty: Failure to pay the monthly Core Benefits to the Qualifying Scheme (or to register an employee within two months, among other duties in Art. 66): fine of up to USD 2,000 for each contravention in respect of each employee (Employment Law Schedule 2). Contributions count as late if not paid by the 21st day of the next calendar month.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Schedule 2: "66(17) Failing to comply with Articles 66(6), (7), (9), (11), (13) and (18), for each contravention in respect of each Employee. $2,000" (maximum fine, USD)
fixes.dueText: Monthly: the Core Benefits for each month must be paid to the Qualifying Scheme by the 21st day of the next calendar month.
fixes.confirmEvidence: an Employer shall be in contravention of Article 66(7) if Core Benefits in respect of any monthly period are not paid by the Employer by the twenty first (21st) day of the next calendar month (DIFC Employment Law, Art. 66(17))

fixes.penalty: Abu Dhabi: late renewal of an economic licence incurs late-renewal fines (amount not stated on the official pages read). Unrenewed licences are moved to an expired registry, and a licence expired for three years or more becomes subject to revocation. A waiver of outstanding late-renewal fines ran for three months until 15 August 2026.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: "Under Abu Dhabi regulations, licences that remain unrenewed are moved to an expired registry. Once a licence has been expired for three or more years, it becomes subject to revocation."
fixes.note: Abu Dhabi only. The 2026 waiver (Abu Dhabi Media Office, 8 Sep 2026): exemption from outstanding late-renewal fines "which ran for three months until 15 August 2026". Other emirates were not read.
fixes.notFound: The licence term and the late-renewal fine amounts were not stated on any official page read. added.gov.ae's licensing page gives no term; Dubai and other emirates' licensing pages were not readable.

fixes.note: Example, DMCC only (its revised late renewal fee FAQ): expired 0-30 days AED 0; 31-60 days AED 2,500; 61-90 days AED 5,000; over 90 days the licence is terminated by the authority.
fixes.notFound: Each free zone sets its own renewal rules and late fees; the u.ae free zone page states neither a licence term nor a fee. Not every zone was read.

fixes.penalty: Renewal up to 30 days after expiry: no fine. Later than 30 days: an automatic fine (maximum USD 25,000 for failing to renew the licence). Failing to file the Confirmation Statement with the renewal: automatic fine of up to USD 10,000. The Registrar may waive the fine on a late renewal.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Schedule 2, Part 1 Automatic fines: "9(11) Person failing to renew its Licence $25,000"; "16(3) Registered Person failing to file a Confirmation Statement as required $10,000" (maximum fine, USD).
fixes.note: Operating Regulations 2.9.3 (in force 27 Dec 2023): a late application "within thirty (30) days of the date of its expiry ... no fine will be applied"; "after thirty (30) days ... an automatic fine will be applied, as specified in Article 9(11)". The fixed amount actually charged is not stated; the law gives maximums. Operating Law text read is the March 2022 consolidation.

fixes.notFound: rakicc.com refused automated access (Incapsula bot check) on both the renewals FAQ and its corporate tax document; no other official page states the RAK ICC renewal rules or late fees.

fixes.penalty: Failure to establish the Register of Beneficial Owners and maintain its data: first time a written warning to correct within 30 days; second time AED 50,000 and a warning; third time AED 100,000. Failure to properly register beneficial ownership details: warning (15 days), then AED 20,000, then AED 40,000. On a third violation the Registrar may also suspend the commercial licence.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Schedule item 3: "Failure of the legal person to establish the Register of Beneficial Owners and maintain its data" - first time written warning (30 days), second time AED (50.000), third time AED (100.000).
fixes.note: Penalties are from the schedule to Cabinet Resolution No. 132 of 2023, read in an English copy published by Dubai Humanitarian (a Dubai licensing registrar), because moet.gov.ae served its legislation list only through a script and uaelegislation.gov.ae returned 403. Cabinet Decision No. 109 of 2023, Art. 18 (read on moet.gov.ae), confirms penalties come from a Cabinet list. Article 3(2): after a third violation the Registrar may also suspend the commercial licence and close the store until the fine is paid and the violation corrected.

fixes.penalty: Failure to update the Register of Beneficial Owners: first time a written warning to correct within 15 days; second time AED 15,000 and a warning; third time AED 30,000. On a third violation the Registrar may also suspend the commercial licence.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Schedule item 4: "Failure of the legal person to update the Register of Beneficial Owners" (Article 8/1) - first time written warning within 15 days, second time AED (15.000), third time AED (30.000).
fixes.note: Penalties are from the schedule to Cabinet Resolution No. 132 of 2023, read in an English copy published by Dubai Humanitarian (a Dubai licensing registrar), because moet.gov.ae served its legislation list only through a script and uaelegislation.gov.ae returned 403. Cabinet Decision No. 109 of 2023, Art. 18 (read on moet.gov.ae), confirms penalties come from a Cabinet list. Article 3(2): after a third violation the Registrar may also suspend the commercial licence and close the store until the fine is paid and the violation corrected.

fixes.penalty: Failure to register on goAML "may result in severe penalties" imposed by the Ministry of Economy and Tourism. The page gives no amount.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: "Failure to register on goAML may result in severe penalties invoked by the Ministry of Economy & Tourism."

fixes.notFound: The Dubai Customs service page states no penalty for not holding a customs code (registration is a precondition of clearing goods, not a filing with a late fee); no official page stating one was found.
No other emirate's customs registration page was read (Abu Dhabi Customs and Sharjah Customs pages were not found in a form that could be opened); no penalty found.

fixes.confirmEvidence: "Since 2024, private sector companies with a workforce of 20 to 49 workers were required to hire at least one UAE citizen by end of 2024. Additionally, they are required to hire one more Emirati by end of 2025."
fixes.note: The page (updated 15 Oct 2026) still states targets only to the end of 2025 and gives the contributions for non-compliance: AED 96,000 in January 2025 for failing to hire one Emirati in 2024; AED 108,000 in January 2026 for failing to hire two Emiratis in 2025. No 2026 target is stated. mohre.gov.ae reset the connection on every attempt.

fixes.notFound: The u.ae page states no fine. mohre.gov.ae reset the connection on every attempt (several tries during the session), and the u.ae copies of the labour law and MoHRE resolutions returned HTTP 404; no other official page read states it.

The u.ae page states no penalty. mohre.gov.ae reset the connection on every attempt (several tries during the session), and the u.ae copies of the labour law and MoHRE resolutions returned HTTP 404; no other official page read states it.

fixes.dueText: Most work permits are valid for two years (a juvenile permit for one year, a national trainee permit for 12 months). Renew before the permit expires; renewal requires the issue conditions to be met, the documents provided and the fees paid by company classification.
fixes.confirmEvidence: "Work permit to recruit a worker from outside the UAE ... The permit is valid for two years." Renewal: "The conditions required for issuance must be met ... Fees must be paid according to the type of permit and the company's classification"
fixes.note: Our dueText says renewal requires settling fines for late issuance or non-renewal; on the current page (updated 19 Oct 2026) that step is listed under CANCELLING a work permit, not renewing. The page gives no renewal window. Fees for issue and renewal are AED 250 to AED 3,450 by company class (A, B or C).
fixes.notFound: No fine amount is on the u.ae page; it refers to Cabinet Resolution No. 21 of 2020 on service fees and administrative fines, whose PDF on u.ae returned HTTP 404, and mohre.gov.ae reset the connection on every attempt.

fixes.penalty: Failure to submit a DPMSR within the predefined parameters and timelines exposes the dealer to enforcement action. The guidance gives no amount.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: "Failure to submit a DPMSR within the predefined parameters and timelines may undermine the effectiveness of the entity's compliance framework and exposes it to enforcement action."
fixes.confirmEvidence: DPMS must file a DPMSR for cash transactions with individuals of AED 55,000 or more, and for transactions with companies/entities of AED 55,000 or more "whether in cash or through wire transfer"; no number of days is stated.
fixes.note: For a sale to a company, cash and wire transfers of AED 55,000 or more both count. For a sale to an individual, only cash of AED 55,000 or more counts. The guidance states no number of days for filing the report.

fixes.penalty: Failure to submit REARs within the predefined parameters and timelines may expose real estate agents and brokers to regulatory action. The guidance gives no amount.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: "Failure to submit REARs within the predefined parameters and timelines may undermine the effectiveness of the entity compliance framework ... and expose Real Estate Agents and Brokers to regulatory action."
fixes.confirmEvidence: "All real estate brokers and agents is required to file a REAR for: Purchase or Sale of freehold property / real estate where the method of payment includes cash and the amount is AED 55,000 or more" (or any virtual-asset payment or conversion).
fixes.note: Confirmed as stated; the time limit is still not given (uaefiu.gov.ae returned HTTP 403).

fixes.notFound: Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2021 sets no fine for this article itself. Art. 362 says the Cabinet will issue a list of administrative penalties (fines of AED 100 to AED 10,000,000, doubled on repetition up to AED 20,000,000); that list was not found on an official page (uaelegislation.gov.ae returned 403, moet.gov.ae lists legislation only through a script).

fixes.penalty: A company that fails to comply with the accounts requirements of Art. 124 (including filing them with the Registrar) is liable to a fine of up to USD 10,000.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Schedule 2: "124(8) Company failing to meet requirements relating to accounts $10,000" (maximum fine, USD); Art. 124(8): "A Company which fails to comply with each of the requirements in this Article 124 is liable to a fine".
fixes.note: The DIFC Companies Law as read (consolidated March 2022) and the DIFC handbook of September 2026 give different periods for accounts. Confirm the period with the DIFC Registrar of Companies before relying on this date.

fixes.penalty: A company that fails to comply with the accounts requirements of Art. 124 is liable to a fine of up to USD 10,000.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Schedule 2: "124(8) Company failing to meet requirements relating to accounts $10,000" (maximum fine, USD); Art. 124(8): "A Company which fails to comply with each of the requirements in this Article 124 is liable to a fine".
fixes.note: The DIFC Companies Law as read (consolidated March 2022) and the DIFC handbook of September 2026 give different periods for accounts and the law exempts small private companies from filing. Confirm the period with the DIFC Registrar of Companies before relying on this date.

fixes.penalty: Failing to notify the Registrar of a change in Registered Details: fine of up to USD 2,000 (Operating Law). Failing to file a special resolution (or other resolution or agreement under Art. 19) within 30 days: fine of up to USD 5,000 (Companies Law). Where no time limit is set, notices are due within 30 days of the event (Operating Regulations 7.2).
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Operating Law Schedule 2, Part 2: "15(2) Company failing to notify the Registrar of a change in Registered Details $2,000"; Companies Law Schedule 2: "19(4) Company failing to file a resolution or agreement with the Registrar $5,000".
fixes.note: Maximum fines in USD. Other registers (e.g. directors and secretaries, Companies Law 82(5): up to USD 2,000; shareholders 44(2): up to USD 10,000) carry their own fines.

fixes.penalty: The employee is entitled to a penalty equal to one daily wage for each day the employer is late with the payments due within 14 days of termination. It can only be awarded if a court holds the unpaid amount to exceed the employee's weekly wage, and a court waives it for any period while a dispute about the amount is pending or where the employee's unreasonable conduct caused the non-payment (Art. 19(2)-(4)).
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Art. 19(2): "an Employee shall be entitled to and the Employer shall pay a penalty equal to an Employee's Daily Wage for each day the Employer is in arrears of its payment obligations under Article 19(1)."

fixes.penalty: Failing to register with the Commissioner by filing a notification of processing operations: fine of up to USD 25,000 (Data Protection Law, Schedule 2, Art. 14(7)).
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Schedule 2: "14(7) Failing to register with the Commissioner in accordance with Article 14(7) of the Law $25,000" (maximum fine, USD).
fixes.dueText: Within 6 months from the incorporation date.
fixes.confirmEvidence: Data Protection Notification: Within 6 months from the Incorporation date (DIFC handbook DIFC-CS-GL-12, revision 6, approved 29 September 2026).

fixes.penalty: Art. 14(7) requires the notification to be "kept up to date through amended notifications"; failing to register in accordance with Art. 14(7): fine of up to USD 25,000.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Art. 14(7): notification "shall be kept up to date through amended notifications". Schedule 2: "14(7) Failing to register with the Commissioner in accordance with Article 14(7) of the Law $25,000".
fixes.note: The Schedule 2 item names Art. 14(7) as a whole; no item names the annual renewal separately. The DIFC FAQ says the first DPO annual assessment is filed on the licence renewal date, which supports (but does not state) renewal with the licence.

fixes.penalty: Failing to report a personal data breach in accordance with Art. 41: fine of up to USD 50,000.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: Schedule 2: "41 Failing to report Personal Data Breach in accordance with Article 41 of the Law $50,000" (maximum fine, USD).

fixes.penalty: Non-compliance with the requirement to file annual accounts may result in regulatory action, including financial penalties of up to USD 15,000 against the company or LLP and against a director or partner, and/or cancellation of the commercial licence.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: "Non-compliance with the requirement to file annual accounts may result in regulatory action, including financial penalties of up to USD 15,000 against the ADGM Company or LLP and director or partner, and/or commercial licence cancellation."
fixes.note: Circular dated 12 April 2023, citing section 416 of the Companies Regulations 2020. The Registrar may approve an extension if applied for before the due date (ADGM annual accounts page).

fixes.notFound: The ADGM pages read state no fine, and the ADGM legislation site (en.adgm.thomsonreuters.com / adgmen.thomsonreuters.com) that hosts the Data Protection Regulations 2021 returned HTTP 403.
The ADGM pages read state no fine, and the ADGM legislation site (en.adgm.thomsonreuters.com / adgmen.thomsonreuters.com) that hosts the Data Protection Regulations 2021 returned HTTP 403.
The DMCC guideline (29 April 2025) states no penalty; no DMCC page stating a fine for late audited statements was found. Figures on non-official sites were not used.
The JAFZA guide page states neither a deadline nor a penalty, and no other JAFZA page stating one was found.

fixes.penalty: An entity that fails to submit, or submits late, is sent an official letter. Missing the timescales for two consecutive reporting periods, or two or more in a calendar year, leads to a meeting with the sector regulatory authority (with top management present) to agree corrective action. Ongoing non-compliance leads the authority to review the entity's OSH management system approval certificate. No fine is stated.
fixes.penaltyEvidence: "Entities who fail to submit or submit late shall be sent an official letter ... Ongoing non-compliance from entities shall result in the SRA reviewing the entity's OSHMS approval certificate"

fixes.notFound: ADOSH-SF Mechanism 11.0 (read) states the notification and investigation timescales but no penalty or fine; no other ADPHC page stating one was read.
